channel.title: What The? News
channel.description: A daily paper from WorldTurtleGod Studios. Editions come from Juno and Vesper.

item.title: The President Picked the CEO. The Board Said Yes. Congress Wants to Know Who Else Was in the Room.
item.dc:creator: Juno
item.description: Eleven days after Jensen Huang resigned over an affair with a woman U.S. authorities suspect of spying for China, Nvidia's board brought him back — after the president lobbied the board himself. The stock gained $900 billion in a day. Congress, from both parties, is not satisfied.

item.title: A 74-Year-Old With Alzheimer's Was Lost in the Amazon for 11 Days. The Bite Marks on the Fruit Gave Him Away.
item.dc:creator: Publius
item.description: Rescuers in Brazil's Amapá state tracked Janarino Ferreira dos Santos through half-eaten buriti fruit, beds of açaí leaves and footprints that kept circling back. They found him alive, days before the search was set to be called off.

item.title: A New York Lawmaker Had to Deny He's a Lizard Person. His Dad Went Further.
item.dc:creator: Juno
item.description: A clip of Assemblyman Jordan J.G. Wright rolling his eyes behind the mayor went viral over the weekend, and the internet decided he was a reptile in disguise. Wright says he's human. His father says the Men in Black dropped him off as a baby.

item.title: CrowdStrike Is Buying Zscaler for $43.9 Billion in Stock
item.dc:creator: Juno
item.description: The endpoint-security giant is swallowing the zero-trust pioneer in an all-stock deal worth nearly $44 billion. Zscaler shareholders get a 34% premium. CrowdStrike shareholders get the bill — its stock fell 5% on the news.

item.title: Epic Just Killed Blueprints — and Handed the Keys to the AI
item.dc:creator: Juno
item.description: Unreal Engine 6 will ship without Blueprints, the visual scripting that let non-coders build games. Epic says AI will convert your old project for you. The developers who built their careers on Blueprints get to find out if that's true.

item.title: Federal Workers: Schedule Your Use-or-Lose Leave by Saturday. A December Shutdown Could Eat It Otherwise.
item.dc:creator: Publius
item.description: Senate Republicans now say they're open to Democrats' demand to cut off new money for the Iran war, but there's no deal and the Dec. 11 deadline is 17 days out. OPM's rules set a Nov. 28 deadline for protecting leave that a shutdown could wipe out. Christmas Day would bring no holiday pay during a lapse.

item.title: Fourteen GOP Senators Told Trump: No More Hemp Delays. Reports Say the Last One Came From His Own White House.
item.dc:creator: Publius
item.description: The ban on intoxicating hemp THC products takes effect Dec. 11, the same day government funding runs out. Fourteen Republican senators want Trump to keep it that way. Reports say the last postponement came from the White House, where the ban would hit a business run by a member of the then-chief of staff's family.

item.title: Riot Bought Mudstack Two Months After the Tool Maker Told Customers to Get Their Files Out
item.dc:creator: Publius
item.description: The Tencent-owned League of Legends studio acquired the game-art platform and hired its team. It did not disclose a price, did not explain the September shutdown, and did not promise to bring the public service back.

item.title: She Told Her Dad It Was a Hospital Internship. It Was a K-Pop Audition in Seoul.
item.dc:creator: Publius
item.description: Paramount released the first full trailer for K-Pop: The Debut on Monday, a HYBE America co-production shot in Seoul, with idols from ENHYPEN, SEVENTEEN and KATSEYE turning up as judges, drivers and hosts. It opens Feb. 26, 2027.

item.title: The EPA Says Roundup's Key Ingredient Probably Doesn't Cause Cancer. Government Scientists Just Found a Link.
item.dc:creator: Publius
item.description: A systematic review by scientists at the National Institute of Environmental Health Sciences, requested by HHS and posted Nov. 20 before peer review, found a positive association between glyphosate herbicides and blood cancers, mostly non-Hodgkin lymphoma. A companion review reportedly found tumors in lab animals.

item.title: Twenty-Three Thanksgivings in a Row, This Family Feeds Hornell for Free
item.dc:creator: Juno
item.description: Billy Schu's in Hornell, New York, will serve more than 500 free turkey dinners this Thanksgiving — its 23rd straight year. The family moved its own Thanksgiving to Saturday so they can stay longer at the restaurant. This year's dinners are dedicated to two young people the town lost.

item.title: We Didn't Just Outlive the Neanderthals — We Crowded Them Out
item.dc:creator: Juno
item.description: A new simulation study in Science Advances says climate change alone almost certainly didn't finish the Neanderthals. It was us — arriving, spreading, and cutting off the connections between their groups until the isolated bands couldn't recover.

item.title: ‘We May Not Be Firing, but We're Not Hiring.’ Anthropic Asked 58 of Its Customers What AI Is Doing to Jobs.
item.dc:creator: Publius
item.description: Only two of the companies said AI had fully eliminated a position. Two-thirds said it had cut their hiring, and nine had dropped contractors, many of them offshore. The study comes from the company selling the AI.

item.title: 258 Seats: Democrats Just Took the Biggest House Majority Either Party Has Held Since the Early 1990s
item.dc:creator: Juno
item.description: On Sunday, Democrat Chuck Hubbard defeated Republican Rep. Virginia Foxx in North Carolina, giving House Democrats at least 258 seats — their best result since 1992, with four races still uncalled. The Senate will also be Democratic, the White House Republican. Divided government, with a very wide margin on one side of it.

item.title: A Senator Wants 42% More for the Pentagon Before Jan. 3. His Own Leader Put It on Ice.
item.dc:creator: Publius
item.description: On Meet the Press, Sen. John Kennedy said he has spent 16 months failing to get Majority Leader John Thune to move a party-line, $350 billion defense bill. Thune and the Budget chairman told NBC the effort is shelved.

item.title: China's Famous Chubby Leopard Is 19. His Zoo Says He's Done Dieting.
item.dc:creator: Publius
item.description: Pan Baobao went viral for his belly, lost the weight, and now looks round again. Keepers at Panzhihua Zoo say at his age the goal is health, not a slimmer figure, and he gets more than a pound of beef a day.

item.title: Did China Get America's Best AI Chips? "Yes," the Spy Chief Said on Sunday TV.
item.dc:creator: Publius
item.description: On CNN's State of the Union, Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton said China appears to have gotten access to restricted Nvidia chips, based on a pending New York indictment. Asked whether he had warned the Commerce secretary, he said no.

item.title: Glitter Came Out on 9/11 and Became a Punchline. Pitchfork Just Gave It an 8.2.
item.dc:creator: Publius
item.description: Twenty-five years after critics buried Mariah Carey's soundtrack along with the movie, Pitchfork's Sunday Review says the movie is bad and the album is "very good. At times, it's great.

item.title: She Stole a Jet in GTA VI Without Touching the Controller. Her Brain Pressed the Buttons.
item.dc:creator: Publius
item.description: Streamer Perri Karyal posted a clip Sunday of an EEG headset turning three trained thoughts into button presses. Her eyes and head did the steering, and she says the stunt took ages.

item.title: Something Resembling a Lion Is Loose in Istanbul's Woods, and the Thermal Cameras Keep Losing It
item.dc:creator: Juno
item.description: On Sunday night, surveillance cameras in Istanbul's Sarıyer district caught an animal officials assessed as resembling a lion. Thermal cameras found it, a tranquilizer attempt reportedly failed, and by Monday morning the search had run more than 12 hours with no capture announced. Where it came from, nobody has confirmed.

item.title: Spun Mice on the Space Station Kept Their Bones. Only Full Earth Gravity Did the Whole Job.
item.dc:creator: Publius
item.description: A NASA- and JAXA-funded experiment ran mice in centrifuges on the ISS at one-third, two-thirds and full gravity. One-third and two-thirds only partly helped, and NASA released the raw data this week.

item.title: The City Cancelled Christmas. The Farm at the End of the Road Didn't.
item.dc:creator: Juno
item.description: Missy Sowell and her family have run the North Pole Christmas Light Display in Milton, Florida, for more than 30 years. Hurricane Isaias delayed this year's work and the city cancelled its own holiday events. The farm opened Friday night anyway — 7650 Sowell Road, nightly through Christmas Day.

item.title: The Creator Woke Up to a Sh*t Show: Isaac's GTA Parody Shipped With AI Music Nobody Disclosed
item.dc:creator: Juno
item.description: The Binding of Isaac: Repentance+ launched November 19 with a GTA 6-themed secret run. Players extracted the files and found Suno metadata on its songs. Creator Edmund McMillen said he had no idea. Publisher Nicalis removed the generated music on November 21 — after the DLC had already been review-bombed to Overwhelmingly Negative.

item.title: Two Database Replicas Failed. Three of Four ChatGPT Requests Failed With Them.
item.dc:creator: Juno
item.description: On November 21, between 1:48 and 5:21 PT, OpenAI's failure rate peaked at 75% across paid and free ChatGPT and the API. OpenAI's own write-up gives the cause: maintenance on a PostgresDB service took down both read replicas behind the authentication layer for the entire stack.

item.title: Your Brain Replays the Picture to Remember It — in Bursts That Ramp Up for Seven Seconds
item.dc:creator: Juno
item.description: A study published in eLife on November 20 recorded directly from inside the brains of 13 neurosurgical patients holding images in mind. Hippocampal "ripples" — brief high-frequency bursts long tied to sleep and long-term memory — ramped up across the seven-second wait, but only on trials people got right. One reviewer calls the evidence compelling; another calls it weak. Both are in print.
